title: World of Wonder: The Story of Candy
description: Bài đọc về lịch sử, định nghĩa và ý nghĩa văn hóa của kẹo qua các thời kỳ.
passage:
WORLD OF WONDER: THE STORY OF CANDY
Exploring the realms of history, science, nature and technology

Paragraph A
The word "candy" is derived from the Arabic word qandi, which means "something made with sugar." Sugary treats are categorized as confections, and a confectioner is a professional who specializes in crafting these sweets. By definition, candy is a sweet confection made with sugar, alternative sweeteners, and artificial or natural flavors. Confectionery items encompass a broad variety of hard candies, lollipops, candy bars, chocolate, and candy floss. However, conventional desserts such as ice cream, cakes, and puddings are not classified as confections.

Paragraph B
Historically, honey was likely the first sweet snack enjoyed by prehistoric humans. Thousands of years ago, ancient Egyptians combined fruits, nuts, and honey to create early forms of candy. In fact, archaeologists have discovered marshmallow and licorice treats inside the tombs of pharaohs. Honey remained the dominant sweetener until sugar cane was first cultivated in ancient China, India, and Persia around A.D. 500. Sugar made its way to Europe around A.D. 1100. Later, in 1519, Spanish explorers in Mexico discovered cacao, the foundation of chocolate. Initially, chocolate was served not as a sweet bar, but as a medicinal beverage. The solid chocolate bar was not invented until the late 1870s.

Paragraph C
Beyond being an indulgence, many early sweets were consumed primarily as medical treatments for digestive issues. Modern items like cough drops and peppermint sticks trace their origins back to this healthcare tradition. Licorice root mixed with honey or sugar was historically used to treat arthritis, asthma, constipation, fatigue, and sore throats.

Paragraph D
Candies have also developed strong cultural connections to holidays. In 1868, Richard Cadbury created the first Valentine candy box, which featured a painting of his daughter and her kitten. Early American colonists made romantic treats by scratching love notes directly onto candy. Today, around 8 billion candy hearts are produced annually with inscriptions such as "Be Mine" and "Kiss Me". Similarly, during the four weeks preceding Christmas, nearly 2 billion candy canes are sold in the United States alone.

fillInBlank: Long before modern factories existed, prehistoric humans satisfied their sweet cravings using ___honey___. As civilizations developed, Egyptians combined this natural sweetener with fruits and nuts, while archaeologists even discovered sweet treats in pharaohs' tombs. In addition to being enjoyed as food, ancient sweets frequently served as treatments for ___digestive___ problems. For example, herbs like licorice were utilized to relieve symptoms such as sore throats and ___fatigue___. Over time, candies became linked with special occasions; early American ___colonists___ wrote romantic messages directly onto sweets. Today, manufactured items often feature printed ___inscriptions___ on heart-shaped candies during holidays.
